sprint.goal: Build a lightweight Kanban project management app: REST API + minimal web UI. Users can create tasks, move them between Todo, In Progress, and Done, edit task details, and delete tasks.

tasks.title: Create tasks table schema (id, title, status, created_at)
Implement REST API: create/list/update/delete tasks, move between statuses
Build Kanban board UI (3 columns, drag or click-to-move) consuming the API
Define API, task lifecycle, and integration contract
Implement Python-standard-library REST API for task CRUD and column moves
Implement a single static HTML vanilla-JS Kanban UI
Implement SQLite task schema and persistence layer
Create and run functional API/UI verification for CRUD and task movement
Review HTTP input handling, SQLite access, and static-file serving security
Create `database.py` containing SQLite connection setup, schema initialization, and task repository functions; own only this file and the runtime `.db` file.
Create `server.py` containing the `http.server` request router, JSON responses, static-file serving, and REST handlers; call the repository API from `database.py` without editing it.
Create `index.html` as the sole static frontend file with vanilla JS for loading, creating, editing, moving, and deleting tasks through `/api/tasks`; do not edit Python files.

messages.content: Provide the contract promptly so implementation work can align.
Proceed with a standard-library-only REST API; await architecture guidance if needed.
Proceed with a single-file vanilla-JS UI and align to the API contract when available.
Architecture contract is ready: SQLite repository (`database.py`), HTTP server (`server.py`), and single-file UI (`index.html`) have exclusive ownership boundaries.

REST contract: GET /api/tasks; POST /api/tasks body {title,description?,status?}; PUT /api/tasks/{id} body may include title,description,status; DELETE /api/tasks/{id}. Return task objects {id,title,description,status,created_at,updated_at}; statuses are todo, in_progress, done.
Use the contract GET/POST /api/tasks and PUT/DELETE /api/tasks/{id}; display statuses todo, in_progress, done as Todo, In Progress, Done. Send JSON and refresh state after mutations.

Repository contract should expose initialize_database(), list_tasks(), create_task(title, description, status), update_task(id, fields), and delete_task(id). Validate/persist only statuses todo, in_progress, done.

Backend is blocked: `database.py` has not been created by the database owner, and the backend ownership boundary requires server handlers to call that repository rather than duplicate persistence logic.
Please provide `database.py` with the agreed repository functions so I can implement `server.py` against it.

Frontend work is complete in the existing `static/index.html`, `static/app.js`, and `static/styles.css`. It renders Todo/In Progress/Done and supports all requested mutations; runtime verification awaits the blocked backend.
The existing UI sends PATCH for partial edits/status moves (rather than PUT). Please support PATCH alongside PUT as noted in your backend decision.

architecture_decisions.decision: Python stdlib http.server + sqlite3 for backend, single static HTML+vanilla JS file for frontend. No external dependencies (sandbox has no network access).
Use Python standard library only, with sqlite3 for persistence and a single static HTML frontend.
Keep the API and UI lightweight with no external packages or build tooling.
Use Python `http.server` for REST routing and static serving, `sqlite3` for persistence, and `json` for payloads/responses; no external packages.
Store tasks in SQLite with id, title, description, status, created_at, and updated_at. Title is required; description defaults to empty; status defaults to `todo`.
Serve `index.html` from the same origin as the API to avoid CORS requirements.
API errors use JSON with an `error` field and appropriate 400, 404, or 405 status codes.
The task lifecycle permits moving directly among `todo`, `in_progress`, and `done`; any invalid status is rejected with 400.
Backend will implement `server.py` only and will not duplicate SQLite persistence code owned by the database role.
The server will accept PATCH as well as PUT for task updates to support the existing static frontend; both use the same partial-update contract.
Retain the existing static UI implementation because it satisfies the requested functionality without external dependencies.
Use PATCH for partial task updates in the UI; backend compatibility with PATCH is required before end-to-end verification.
